decisions.reason: The digital anamnesis app was launched as a flagship new product line and fits the post-pandemic push toward digitising dental practices, so it likely meets aspirations and remains part of the core offering.

The continuing education institute builds on the firm's established dental-practice customer base and its training infrastructure, and with the firm's slack it costs little to keep while supporting customer loyalty.
The remote support tool is a low-cost service enabler that became more valuable with remote work, so there is no performance shortfall to trigger dropping it.
The analytics dashboard extends the core practice-management software and uses its data, so although adoption is uncertain the firm's slack lets it carry the product.
The complete practice bundle is mainly a packaging of existing offerings and may be reconfigured, but full withdrawal within a year is less likely than keeping it.

The job and practice listing portal lies furthest from the core business and faces strong competitors, which makes it the most likely candidate for problemistic search, yet its low running cost probably keeps it alive for now.
